genZNote: Intrinsically fluconazole-resistant right out of the gate — no acquired mutation needed, it just never worked to begin with.

morphology.shape: Elongated oval budding yeast cells, forms pseudohyphae

habitat.naturalHabitat: Human gastrointestinal tract as commensal flora; also found in fermented foods and beverages
habitat.hostAssociation: Opportunistic pathogen, particularly in patients with hematologic malignancy or prior azole prophylaxis
habitat.environmentalOccurrence: Found in soil, fermenting fruit, and some fermented food/beverage production
habitat.reservoir: Human GI tract and environmental sources

microscopy.stain: Gram stain or KOH wet mount

culture.pigmentation: Pink, rough-edged colonies on CHROMagar Candida

identificationClues: Germ tube negative, elongated budding yeast forming pseudohyphae
Rough, spreading, 'fuzzy' colonies on CHROMagar Candida (distinct from smooth C. albicans/C. glabrata colonies)
Intrinsically resistant to fluconazole — a defining clinical feature of this species
Risk factor: prior fluconazole prophylaxis, especially in neutropenic/hematologic malignancy patients

diseases: Candidemia and invasive candidiasis, particularly in neutropenic patients or those on fluconazole prophylaxis
Oropharyngeal and esophageal candidiasis in immunocompromised hosts
virulenceFactors: Intrinsic resistance to fluconazole via reduced drug affinity for its target enzyme
clinicalImportance.transmission: Usually endogenous from the patient's own GI flora; can also spread via contaminated hands/devices in healthcare settings
clinicalImportance.epidemiology: Classically emerges as a breakthrough Candida infection in patients receiving fluconazole prophylaxis (e.g., hematology/oncology and stem cell transplant patients), given its intrinsic azole resistance
clinicalImportance.labSignificance: Because resistance is intrinsic (not just acquired), fluconazole should never be used empirically once C. krusei is identified or strongly suspected — echinocandins or voriconazole are preferred

examFacts.importantDisease: Candidemia, especially breakthrough infection during fluconazole prophylaxis
examFacts.importantTest: Species identification (intrinsic fluconazole resistance changes antifungal choice)
examFacts.distinguishingFeature: Intrinsically fluconazole-resistant Candida species that classically breaks through in patients already on fluconazole prophylaxis
